case.suppression: The requesters asked for confidentiality for fear of retaliation.
case.title: Tümad Gold Mines: Villagers Lose Grazing Land
case.point: Değirmenbaşı, İvrindi district (coordinates from Wikipedia). The complaint record does not name the mine; the village name matches İvrindi, site of one of the two Tümad mines. Approximate.

lenders.name: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development
lenders.role: 40 million euro loan for Tümad's Lapseki (Çanakkale) and Ivrindi (Balıkesir) gold mines, project 49041, part of a US$200 million package with Akbank and Ziraat Bankası as parallel lenders.

case.conditions: Bank loan to Tümad, a subsidiary of Nurol Holding, for mine development. The project planned vocational training and new jobs as alternative income.
case.community: About 372 villagers from Değirmenbaşı told the bank's complaint office on 23 August 2020 that mining had taken over their grazing lands, so they could no longer live from livestock, and that the promised training and jobs did not materialise (EBRD IPAM).
case.outcome: They asked only for problem-solving. The process ended on 7 September 2022 with no agreement (EBRD); Accountability Console records the complaint as withdrawn. No compliance review took place, so no office has ruled on the harm.

case.title: TIPNIS road, signed Brazilian loan: police break up the Chaparina march
case.place: La Chaparina, near Yucumo, Beni, Bolivia
case.point: Camp of the Eighth Indigenous March at La Chaparina, near Yucumo (approximate)

lenders.name: Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES)
lenders.role: Signed a loan contract for up to US$332 million on 15 February 2011, approved by Bolivia's Law 112 of 7 May 2011, so it was in force at the 25 September 2011 police action. BNDES never released any money for the highway (Mongabay). It cancelled in 2012 (Los Tiempos; Conectas); Mongabay dates the formal end to September 2013.

case.conditions: Loan contract covering 80% of the US$415 million, 306 km Villa Tunari-San Ignacio de Moxos highway. The Brazilian firm OAS held the building contract. Segment II, about 177 km, would have cut through TIPNIS, a national park and indigenous territory (Agência Brasil; Plataforma BNDES statement carried by IHU).
case.community: About 800 marchers, mostly indigenous and including women and children, were attacked on 25 September 2011. Mothers and children were separated and put on eight buses towards Yucumo; a preliminary list from the group Fobomade named dozens missing, including children (Plataforma BNDES statement carried by IHU). Official counts of injured or detained were not found.
case.suppression: About 500 police raided the camp on 25 September 2011 with tear gas and arrested leaders, who were then freed by townspeople of Rurrenabaque (Eurasia Review). The Plataforma BNDES statement adds batons and says the camp was set on fire (IHU). A peer-reviewed study describes armed forces dispersing the march (Contexto Internacional).
case.killed_note: No deaths are reported in these sources.
case.outcome: Four officials resigned, including the defense and government ministers. President Morales denied ordering the operation and apologized. He signed a law suspending the road, reported 27 October 2011 (Eurasia Review; Agência Brasil). Campaigners wrote to BNDES on 25 August 2011 asking it to suspend financing; the Plataforma BNDES reported no reply.

No source says BNDES asked for the police action. BNDES says it met all legal requirements and that the claim it failed in due diligence is incorrect. A study citing a Constitutional Court resolution dates a contract with OAS and BNDES to 2009; a financing protocol was signed on 22 August 2009 (Mongabay).

reason: No Brazilian money was ever released, and the police action was the Bolivian government's.

case.title: In Salah shale gas: Total and Sonatrach drilling, protesters arrested
case.place: In Salah (Ain Salah), Tamanrasset province, Algeria
case.point: Town of In Salah; protesters targeted a Halliburton base about 10 km north

lenders.name: TotalEnergies (then Total; France; foreign company)
lenders.role: Won the Ahnet licence with 47% in December 2009, with Partex at 2% and Sonatrach at 51% (MEED). Multinationales gives Total 49% and says Total and Sonatrach were doing the first shale drilling.

case.conditions: Foreign company, not a loan. Other reports name Sonatrach and the US contractor Halliburton as doing the tests and do not mention Total (Al Jazeera; Vice).

companies.name: Halliburton
companies.role: Contractor with a base near In Salah; not the link here

case.community: Opponents fear groundwater damage to oasis farming (Multinationales). This is a fear and no measured damage was found. The harm recorded here is the crackdown.
case.suppression: Algerian police arrested about 50 demonstrators on 24 February 2015 and hundreds more in following days, using tear gas and rubber bullets (The Ecologist). In clashes outside the Halliburton base on 28 February-1 March, El Watan reported live bullets and 20 protesters treated in hospital (Vice). The interior ministry reported 40 police injured, and protesters burned official buildings and a police truck; an activist reported at least 20 injured in Tamanrasset (The New Arab).
case.killed_note: Protester Mohamed El Noui, 21, died on 4 January 2015 after clashes with security forces (Multinationales). Not counted: no source ties the security forces to the company.
case.outcome: Energy Minister said pollution risk was no greater than conventional fuels and water would be reused (Multinationales). A presidential adviser called shale gas "a gift from God" (The Ecologist).

case.confidence_note: The arrests and shootings were by the Algerian state; no source says Total asked for them, or places Total at the clashes. Only one source says Total was drilling at the time, while its licence stake is confirmed. Pollution harm is feared, not measured.

reason: Pollution was feared rather than measured, and nothing ties the police arrests to Total.
